Mean and median EDTRS lines gain with time.
(A) Fundus photo and OCT before tPA + gas administration
(B) Fundus photo and OCT 14 days after tPA + gas, showing significant reduction in haemorrhage and retinal thickness; the patient received the first intravitreal aflibercept 2 mg
(C) Fundus photo and OCT 1 month postoperatively (only small remnants of blood visible)
(D) Fundus photo and OCT 3 months postoperatively, patient on aflibercept 2 mg T&Ex regimen
(E) Fundus photo and OCT 6 months postoperatively, no blood visible but MNV still active, requiring continuation of anti-VEGF therapy
(A) Fundus photo and OCT before tPA + gas, showing thick sub-macular haemorrhage involving the fovea
(B) Fundus photo and OCT 7 days after tPA + gas, showing marked reduction in haemorrhage and retinal thickness; patient received first intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg
(C) Fundus photo and OCT 1 month postoperatively (thin blood remnants visible)
(D) Fundus photo and OCT 3 months postoperatively, showing foveal atrophy in both fundus image and OCT; patient on aflibercept 8 mg T&Ex regimen
(E) Fundus photo and OCT 6 months postoperatively, no blood visible, with central atrophy and persistent MNV activity requiring ongoing anti-VEGF therapy

limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.
The aflibercept formulation (2 mg or 8 mg) is not stated per patient; no dose is recorded.

Disputed attribution: Results name two eyes with foveal atrophy without case numbers; one sentence names Cases 1 and 9 as late cases with atrophy and limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) that do not match Table 2, while the Discussion pairs Cases 3 and 10 with MNV scarring and says they presented late (up to 2 months) although Table 1 gives 21 and 8 days. Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.

limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.
The aflibercept formulation (2 mg or 8 mg) is not stated per patient; no dose is recorded.

Disputed attribution: Results name two eyes with foveal atrophy without case numbers; one sentence names Cases 1 and 9 as late cases with atrophy and limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) that do not match Table 2, while the Discussion pairs Cases 3 and 10 with MNV scarring and says they presented late (up to 2 months) although Table 1 gives 21 and 8 days. Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.

attribution_limitations: The Discussion says Cases 3 and 10 presented late with haemorrhage duration up to 2 months, but Table 1 gives symptom durations of 21 days (Case 3) and 8 days (Case 10). The same sentence attributes early ellipsoid-zone disruption on OCT to "Both eyes", whose referent is the two atrophic eyes of the preceding sentence or Cases 3 and 10. The text elsewhere names Cases 1 and 9 as the two late cases with atrophy.

The Methods state that aflibercept was either 2.0 mg/0.1 mL or 8 mg/0.1 mL across the cohort, and the Table 2 column header says 7–14 Days Postop. while the Methods say 7 days or 14 days. The formulation and the exact day of the early review are not stated for this patient.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.

limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.
The aflibercept formulation (2 mg or 8 mg) is not stated per patient; no dose is recorded.

Disputed attribution: Results name two eyes with foveal atrophy without case numbers; one sentence names Cases 1 and 9 as late cases with atrophy and limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) that do not match Table 2, while the Discussion pairs Cases 3 and 10 with MNV scarring and says they presented late (up to 2 months) although Table 1 gives 21 and 8 days. Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.

limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.
The aflibercept formulation (2 mg or 8 mg) is not stated per patient; no dose is recorded.

Disputed attribution: Results name two eyes with foveal atrophy without case numbers; one sentence names Cases 1 and 9 as late cases with atrophy and limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) that do not match Table 2, while the Discussion pairs Cases 3 and 10 with MNV scarring and says they presented late (up to 2 months) although Table 1 gives 21 and 8 days. Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.

limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.
The aflibercept formulation (2 mg or 8 mg) is not stated per patient; no dose is recorded.

Disputed attribution: Results name two eyes with foveal atrophy without case numbers; one sentence names Cases 1 and 9 as late cases with atrophy and limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) that do not match Table 2, while the Discussion pairs Cases 3 and 10 with MNV scarring and says they presented late (up to 2 months) although Table 1 gives 21 and 8 days. Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.

limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.
The aflibercept formulation (2 mg or 8 mg) is not stated per patient; no dose is recorded.

Disputed attribution: Results name two eyes with foveal atrophy without case numbers; one sentence names Cases 1 and 9 as late cases with atrophy and limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) that do not match Table 2, while the Discussion pairs Cases 3 and 10 with MNV scarring and says they presented late (up to 2 months) although Table 1 gives 21 and 8 days. Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.

attribution_limitations: The source says Case 9 had transient intraocular pressure elevation that resolved with paracentesis, but the Methods describe a protocol paracentesis after every injection to prevent such elevation. It is not stated whether the paracentesis that resolved the elevation was the protocol paracentesis or an additional one.

The text says the late cases, Case 1 and Case 9, had limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) consistent with atrophy, but the Table 2 BCVA values for this case (before and 6 months) give a different difference. The Results also say two eyes developed atrophy without naming them, and the Discussion names Cases 3 and 10 as the eyes with scarring.

The Methods state that aflibercept was either 2.0 mg/0.1 mL or 8 mg/0.1 mL across the cohort, and the Table 2 column header says 7–14 Days Postop. while the Methods say 7 days or 14 days. The formulation and the exact day of the early review are not stated for this patient.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.
The aflibercept formulation (2 mg or 8 mg) is not stated per patient; no dose is recorded.

Disputed attribution: Results name two eyes with foveal atrophy without case numbers; one sentence names Cases 1 and 9 as late cases with atrophy and limited improvement (0.18 and 0.22 logMAR) that do not match Table 2, while the Discussion pairs Cases 3 and 10 with MNV scarring and says they presented late (up to 2 months) although Table 1 gives 21 and 8 days. Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.

Ten individual eyes are listed only through Table 1 and Table 2 plus a few case-numbered complication statements; the narrative otherwise describes the cohort and is not copied to individuals except where the sentence says all patients or all eyes.

Facts about these are review_only or omitted.

Aggregate inconsistencies are kept as printed and not copied to individuals: mean duration of symptoms 25 days in the text versus 24 in Table 1; patients aged 80 years or more n = 3 in the text versus two in Table 1; mean gains by sex and the statement that none lost vision do not match the Table 2 individual values (Cases 5 and 7 have higher logMAR at 6 months than before).
Table 1 and Table 2 Mean and Median rows are aggregate and are not patient facts.
The Fig 3 and Fig 4 examples are not attributed to any case; the text does not name them. Printed OCT thickness values inside the images are pixel content recorded only in the visual submission.
The fundus photography and SD-OCT facts rely on the protocol sentence worded for Patients together with the sentence that all ten eyes completed the six-month examination schedule.
The Results text writes MNVB scarring and the figure 2 caption writes EDTRS; both kept as printed.
